questions.q: What is the first job when a discrepancy report like Finance's comes in?
options: Reproducing the problem reliably on your own screen, before touching anything
Immediately suspending every Task in the pipeline
Rewriting the MERGE statement to be safe
Deleting the refund_events table and rebuilding it from scratch
questions.explain: Reproducing the reported problem under known conditions comes before any fix — 'it jumped' isn't specific enough to act on.

questions.q: What specific pattern is found in vw_finance_refunds for the affected week?
options: Two rows with the exact same ticket_id and the exact same updated_at timestamp, both counted in the same week's total
A single row with a negative refund_amount
A ticket_id that doesn't exist anywhere in ticket_facts
A refund_amount stored as a text string instead of a number
questions.explain: Duplicate rows sharing both ticket_id and updated_at indicate the same refund event was written twice, not two genuine separate refunds.

questions.q: Why is a genuine second refund expected to carry a different updated_at than the first?
options: Because a real second refund event happens at a different point in time, not the identical timestamp as the original
Snowflake automatically randomizes updated_at on every INSERT
updated_at is unrelated to when a refund actually happened
It isn't expected to differ — two refunds always share the same updated_at
questions.explain: Two rows sharing identical ticket_id AND updated_at can't represent two distinct real-world refund events, since each event has its own timestamp.

questions.q: Why does this lesson treat Support's numbers being unaffected as a useful clue, not just a side note?
options: Because the lead is finance_refund_task's non-idempotent MERGE specifically, and ticket_facts_sync_task's idempotent MERGE would tolerate the same situation without visible harm
Because Support's numbers are always correct regardless of any pipeline issue
Because Support uses a completely different, unrelated Snowflake account
It isn't a useful clue — it's coincidental and unrelated to the cause
questions.explain: Since both Tasks read the same Stream, Support's numbers staying correct while Finance's don't points specifically at a difference between the two Tasks' MERGE logic, not the Stream itself.

questions.q: What does this lesson say NOT to do yet, before Lesson 14?
options: Delete the duplicate rows, rewrite the MERGE, or suspend any Task
Open Finance's page at all
Compare refund_event_count against the distinct ticket count
Check whether the pattern holds across multiple weeks
questions.explain: The lesson has a reproducible symptom and a strong lead, but confirms the actual cause in Lesson 14 before changing anything.
